subject: Physics
description: Bar magnet, Earth's magnetism, electromagnetic induction

questions.explanation: Like poles REPEL, unlike poles ATTRACT. This is the basic law of magnetism (Gilbert). Gauss's law for magnetism says magnetic monopoles don't exist — N and S always come together.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The Earth acts like a giant MAGNET with its magnetic NORTH pole located near:

options.option_text: Geographic South Pole (magnetic N is near geographic S and vice versa)

questions.explanation: Earth's MAGNETIC north pole is actually a 'south' magnetic pole geographically — that's why the north-pointing end of a compass needle (which is a NORTH pole) is attracted there (opposites attract). Terminology is historical. The magnetic poles drift ~55 km/year.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The principle on which an ELECTRIC GENERATOR works is:
questions.explanation: Generator — rotates a coil in a magnetic field → changing flux → induced EMF per Faraday's law (1831). Converts mechanical → electrical energy. Motor is the reverse (electrical → mechanical) based on the same underlying physics but force on current-carrying conductor.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The SI unit of MAGNETIC flux is:
questions.explanation: Weber (Wb) = SI unit of magnetic flux (Φ). Tesla (T) = SI unit of magnetic flux DENSITY (B). Relation: 1 T = 1 Wb/m². Henry (H) = unit of inductance. Gauss — CGS unit for flux density (1 T = 10,000 G).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The materials that are STRONGLY attracted by a magnet are called:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic — strong permanent magnetism; Fe, Co, Ni, Gd. Paramagnetic — weakly attracted (e.g., aluminium, platinum). Diamagnetic — weakly REPELLED (e.g., copper, water). Antiferromagnetic — magnetic moments cancel (e.g., MnO).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The direction of an INDUCED current is given by:

options.option_text: Lenz's law (induced current opposes the change causing it)

questions.explanation: Lenz's law — induced current flows in a direction such that it OPPOSES the change in magnetic flux that caused it. Consequence of energy conservation. Manifested as the 'minus' sign in Faraday's law: ε = −dΦ/dt.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A SOLENOID carrying current behaves similarly to a:

options.option_text: Bar magnet (with one end as N, other as S)

questions.explanation: Solenoid — coiled wire. Carrying current creates a magnetic field like a bar magnet. Polarity determined by right-hand-rule (curl fingers with current flow, thumb points to N). Used in electromagnets, door locks, starter motors, relays.
